title: Pocognoli has 'positive nervousness' for Scotland debut
description: Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli admits to feeling a "positive nervousness" before his first game in charge of the country, a Nations League tie against Slovenia in Ljubljana on Saturday.
body: Sebastien Pocognoli will take charge of Scotland for the first time in Slovenia on Saturday Nations League: Slovenia v Scotland Saturday 26 September, 14:00 BST Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli admits to feeling a "positive nervousness" before his first game in charge of the country, a Nations League tie against Slovenia in Ljubljana on Saturday. The Belgian was appointed in August, replacing Steve Clarke, whose seven-year tenure ended after Scotland's exit at the group stages of the World Cup. Pocognoli starts with four Nations League matches across 11 days, with the trip to Slovenia followed by Switzerland at Hampden, a fixture in North Macedonia, then a return meeting with the Slovenes in Glasgow. "If we talk about nerves, yes, but it's a positive nervousness," he told BBC Sport Scotland. "We have a job with responsibility. It's excitement and I'm just passionate about being on the touchline." Scotland are currently at a warm weather camp in La Manga, Spain with a much-changed squad. Pocognoli has picked a 19-year-old in James Wilson, four 20-year-olds - Findlay Curtis, Ben Gannon-Doak, Lennon Miller and Colby Donovan - and another three aged 22 - Kristi Montgomery, Luke Graham and Robbie Ure. With Blackburn's Montgomery replacing the injured Kenny McLean, there are now eight uncapped players in the squad. "It's a lot of new faces, so it's a challenge to find the right balance, to keep the cohesion in the team," Pocognoli said. Well-travelled Binks eager to make mark for Scotland From leaving Rangers to La Liga - Scotland is next step for Ure McPake's 'colourful' journey from club-less to Scotland call-up in three years This video can not be played Pocognoli on call from Clarke The manager says he knows his team and his formation for the Slovenia game but is not wedded to any particular system, although playing three at the back has been a staple of his coaching to this point. "I always think the players select themselves," he added. "We have four games, so we need to plan. We need to have a periodisation [managing training loads, games and recovery] about the tactical aspect and the physical aspect. "This team can be flexible. We're ready for the four games in terms of what kind of approach we want to give." Pocognoli revealed he has had a conversation with his predecessor, Clarke - "a nice meeting on the phone," as he put it. "He was very kind, very... humble. That was very helpful for me. It just was to let me know that he's behind the team. He was very happy [in his time in the job] but he also felt that it was the right time [to leave]. He wished me all the best. "I will try to be as successful as the previous staff because we want to play in a big tournament. We want to create this moment for the country." Asked if his brand of football will involve more risk and adventure than Clarke's, he said: "We have to find the right balance because if you play fantastic football and you don't qualify you get some criticism." Pocognoli's style is all about aggressive pressing and fast tempo. He says that it might take a while for cohesion to be achieved but there are certain things that he wants to see straight away against Slovenia. "For me, it's about the personality of the players," he added. "I like a unit team who are just fighting for each other. "It's a basic principle - attack together and squeeze the pitch. When we need to defend, it's just to defend like brothers. When we lose the ball, it's try to regain the ball as quickly as possible. "From that, there are a lot of other principles, but that's the base. If you cannot get this, you will never have good principles on the pitch." Given the condensed nature of the games, there is going to be a fair degree of rotation from Slovenia away, to Switzerland at home, to North Macedonia away and Slovenia at home. "So good so far," Pocognoli said about what he has seen in La Manga. "But we need to get the response through the games. It's up to them to perform well, but it's up to me to make them perform well." title: 'It can't be brushed over' - Republic of Ireland squad to discuss Israel games
description: Dara O'Shea says the Republic of Ireland squad will wait until after Thursday's Kosovo game before discussing how they approach Sunday's contentious fixture against Israel.
body: Dara O'Shea says Republic of Ireland players will hold a squad meeting on Friday Dara O'Shea says the Republic of Ireland squad will wait until after Thursday's Kosovo game before discussing how they approach Sunday's contentious fixture against Israel. The Republic of Ireland face Kosovo in Pristina on Thursday (19:45 BST) before travelling to Debrecen in Hungary for the first of two Israel games in this international window. There have been increasing calls in Ireland for a boycott of the matches, with a protest held at the Republic of Ireland team hotel in Dublin on Monday. This followed an open letter by the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, signed by over 160 Irish sportspeople, urging the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) to withdraw from the fixtures because of the situation in Gaza. O'Shea said it is important for the squad to "speak openly" and "respect each other's views" when they come together to discuss the Israel game on Friday. "We've got to respect each other's opinions and each other's views and really sit down and take the time, because it deserves the time to talk about," he said. "It's the main thing and it's something that can't be brushed over. Whatever decision that we go through as players is taken as one and everybody's view is respected as well. O'Shea, who will captain the Republic of Ireland in the absence of the injured Nathan Collins, added the players have been aware of the "noise" surrounding this window but have tried to avoid it as much as possible. "The good thing we have as players is when we step into the squad you're in the international bubble straight away," added the Ipswich defender. "So we've known the noise around the game and there has been, but I think we've all tried to stay off social media as much as possible and stay together." Israel FA comments on Hallgrimsson 'unacceptable' - Martin Neutral venues and no 'away' fans - how Israel v Republic of Ireland became so contentious Uefa rejected request to keep Republic of Ireland and Israel separate - FAI O'Shea admitted it was a "difficult" and "unusual" situation for the players, who will also face Israel in the Republic of Ireland's 'home' game in the Serbian town of Backa Topola on 4 October. "We've got a massive game tomorrow that we've been preparing for," he said. "We've come in on Sunday and our focus straight away was preparing for that game and giving it the amount of effort that it needs. "Kosovo are a great side and we've been preparing for that. We spoke already at the start of the week that we're going to come together on Friday and discuss this as a group. "Tomorrow we've got a game to focus on, first of all. I don't think we'll be doing our job properly if we didn't put our full focus into that game. Once the game's over and Friday comes, we're all going to come together as one." When asked if a boycott of the Israel games will be discussed among the squad on Friday, O'Shea said: "For us, the decision was made by the FAI, Uefa and the Government. For us as players, that's not our decision. "We're Irish players and when called upon we come and represent our country and that's important to know too. "Obviously when we come together, we'll speak openly about what we feel and what we feel is right. And yeah, that'll be given its time on Friday." Hallgrimsson's comments about facing Israel prompted an angry response from the country's football association Earlier this week, Israel's football governing body accused Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimmson of "ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity" regarding comments he made about facing Israel. Last week, Hallgrimsson said: "We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide. We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel." While the FAI did not respond publicly, Taoiseach Micheal Martin [Irish prime minister] said Israel FA's comments were "unacceptable" and "should be withdrawn". Addressing the matter on Wednesday, Hallgrimsson expressed gratitude for the support he has received while admitting "it was not clever" of him to generate headlines in the build-up to the Kosovo match. "Obviously, we are grateful for all the support that we have," said the Icelander, who has been in charge since 2024. "Creating and taking over maybe the headlines at the moment, what I said [in the] last press meeting we had is taking the attention away from maybe what's most important," he said. "We are playing an important game against Kosovo. So that was not the purpose and from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention like this. "I need to be focused on the game, the players need to be focused on the game. But to answer the question, we're thankful for all the support we get. It's a tricky time for us." Armed Palestinian group Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023, killing about 1,200 people and taking 251 hostages. In response, Israel launched a massive military offensive in Gaza, during which more than 73,000 people have been killed, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations. Israel has repeatedly denied that it has committed genocide, as well as war crimes and crimes against humanity. It says its military operations in Gaza have been conducted in self-defence and in accordance with international law. title: Angry Anderson, rock star who soundtracked Kylie's wedding in Neighbours, dies aged 79
description: He fronted the rock band Rose Tattoo, but became best known for his solo hit Suddenly.
body: Rock star Angry Anderson, whose music famously soundtracked the wedding of Kylie Minogue and Jason Donovan's characters in Australian TV soap Neighbours, has died at the age of 79. The musician, whose real name was Gary Anderson, rose to fame as the frontman of Rose Tattoo, one of Australia's most revered rock bands, from 1976. His solo song Suddenly became a global hit after it was played during the wedding of Minogue and Donovan's characters Scott and Charlene in Neighbours. The wedding episode was watched by 20 million people in the UK alone in 1988. Anderson said Minogue had been "adamant" that the track was used for the scene, and he later declared that Suddenly was the best song he had ever written. Before his death, Anderson had a cardiac arrest while on Rose Tattoo's farewell tour in Europe last month. He was treated in hospital before going home to Australia, and the band cancelled nine live dates. A joint statement, external from Anderson's family and Rose Tattoo remembered him as a "devoted father, and much-loved bandmate". "His loss will be deeply felt by all those who knew and loved him both here in Australia and overseas," it said. "We thank everyone for their prayers and messages of love and continued support." Jason Donovan and Kylie Minogue helped propel Neighbours to the height of its popularity Born in Melbourne in 1947, Anderson and Rose Tattoo first became known on Australia's rock scene, releasing five albums beginning with their 1978 debut. After the band split nine years later, Anderson continued recording music as a solo artist, and co-wrote and released Suddenly in the summer of 1987. It was quickly selected by Minogue for use in Neighbours for her character Charlene Mitchell's wedding to Donovan's Scott Robinson. Thanks in large part to its use in Neighbours, Suddenly reached the top three in both the UK and Australia. However, it was held off the number one spot in its home country by Minogue's own debut solo single, Locomotion. Anderson released two albums as a solo artist, before Rose Tattoo reunited in 1993 to support Guns N' Roses on their Australian tour. The band returned in 1998 for their own tour and were inducted into the Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA) Hall of Fame in 2006. Anderson's other credits included playing Herod in an Australian production of Jesus Christ Superstar. He was made a Member of the Order of Australia in 1993, in recognition of service to the community, particularly his charity work and his work as a youth advocate. title: South Sudan's president dissolves government ahead of country's first elections
description: South Sudan has not held elections since independence in 2011 - polls have twice been postponed.
body: Salva Kiir is seeking re-election at the country's first national poll since independence South Sudan President Salva Kiir has dissolved the transitional government, three months before the country's first election since its independence in 2011. The country has previously postponed elections twice and extended the transitional period several times. Under the amended law, signed on Monday, Kiir removed the country's five vice-presidents and dissolved parliament, as well as national and state governments. Kiir is the presidential candidate of his Sudan People's Liberation Movement (SPLM). No prominent figures have announced plans to challenge him in the December poll. The main opposition leader Riek Machar was sacked as vice-president last year and charged with treason. He is under house arrest. Machar had been named vice-president as part of a 2018 peace deal to end a five-year civil war between forces loyal to the two men. Kiir will remain in office with full constitutional powers until an elected president is sworn in. He also reappointed some ministers and governors in caretaker positions until the 22 December elections. Ahead of Tuesday's announcement a heavy security presence was reported in the capital, Juba. Soldiers from the army and national security services blocked access to government ministries. Soldiers were also seen patrolling parts of the city. A senior government official told the BBC that staff arriving for work were turned away and told to return the following Monday. UN agencies in Juba also asked staff to work remotely while the situation was monitored. South Sudan's leader sacks aides after dead man appointed Kiir last week dismissed the chairman of the national elections commission, Abednego Akok Kacuol, without giving a reason. He was replaced by the commission's secretary-general, Gabriel Bol Deng. Akok had said in August that the commission needed $250m (£190m) to conduct the election but had received only $21m. In June, the main opposition group, the Sudan People's Liberation Movement in Opposition (SPLM-IO), the party of Machar, warned people not to take part in poll preparations. "Anyone coming to register voters and campaign in territories controlled by the mighty SPLM-IO, you will be a prisoner of war," Nathaniel Pierino, acting chairperson of the group, said in a post on Facebook. The body which oversees implementation of the 2018 peace agreement, the Reconstituted Joint Monitoring and Evaluation Commission (RJMEC), said South Sudan had entered a "critical phase". It said several key talks under the agreement remained incomplete and urged the parties to agree on a path towards credible elections and a peaceful end to the transitional period, which has lasted since independence. The latest 24-month extension was due to end on 22 February 2027. title: Jorja Smith 'very grateful' as she bags independent music prize
description: The singer reflected on her "crazy" journey as she collected the prize for best independent track.
body: British R&B singer Jorja Smith took home the prize for her 2025 track The Way I Love You Jorja Smith was among the artists recognised at this year's Independent Music Awards for her song The Way I Love You. Accepting the award on Tuesday night at London's Roundhouse, Smith reflected on her "crazy" music journey and took a moment to mark the achievements of artists. "Everyone should be so proud," the Walsall singer said, especially those "doing everything independently". The annual awards celebrate unsigned artists and small record labels. Smith was visibly excited as she accepted her award on stage, while also encouraging the audience to applaud the other nominees and winners. "I'm just very grateful," she told the audience. "I can't believe I've been able to just have this space to create, the same way I've been doing since I was like, 11." Sexistential, the latest record from Swedish singer-songwriter Robyn, was named best independent album at the ceremony, which also honoured 2-Tone heavyweight Pauline Black with the outstanding contribution to music award. Motown inspired musician Jalen Ngonda took home the prize for best breakthrough act, while Jim Legxacy bagged best EP for black British music, which included hit tracks like '06 Wayne Rooney. Best breakthrough act Jalen Ngonda has become known for his soulful style of singing Gee Davy, CEO of the Association of Independent Music which organised the event, said this year's winners demonstrated "extraordinary success" through "collective strength". She credited a "spirit of collaboration" as "a key reason why our members continue to create cultural and commercial value far beyond their scale". title: 'It was scary' – Jacks goes from hospital bed to England match-winner
description: Will Jacks' career-best 50-over figures on Tuesday came shortly after the England all-rounder was rushed into hospital for emergency surgery while on a weekend away.
body: This video can not be played Watch the best of Jacks' match-winning performance as England beat Sri Lanka Will Jacks was supposed to be going to Edinburgh last month to celebrate his mum's 60th birthday. Instead, what the England all-rounder thought was a "tummy bug" turned out to be appendicitis. From there, a rushed visit to the Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh and emergency surgery followed. "It was just really bad really quickly so we had to go," Jacks, 27, said. "It was, obviously, completely random and quite scary. I was lucky to be looked after really well by the NHS." Jacks stars as England grind out win over Sri Lanka Listen to Case Notes podcast: Appendicitis Jacks was given an initial four-week recovery period but ended up returning a few days early to captain the Lions in a warm-up against Sri Lanka on 11 September. Afterwards he played in all three T20s in England's series sweep against the same opponents, and on Tuesday took career-best 50-over figures of 5-22 in the first one-day international in Chester-le-Street. "Luckily they were able to do a slight incision and not have to rip me open completely," he said. Appendix operations are not rare but they do not fit naturally with the twisting and turning of a spin bowler's action, meaning Jacks has been doing extra work behind the scenes to rebuild his core strength. It makes the 4.3 degrees of turn Jacks found at Chester-le-Street – the most he has produced at home in his ODI career – even more impressive, albeit helped by a slow pitch. His figures were also the second best by an England spinner in one-day internationals. "It was more of a confidence thing," he said. "It helped that we were playing the T20s first and I was bowling a maximum of four overs. "If I am honest, I only bowled five days before the first game because I was building up my strength and trying to get some fitness back. "I didn't bowl too much in the T20 series, which probably benefited me. It has been OK." This video can not be played Highlights - Jacks stars for England as they beat Sri Lanka in first ODI Jacks' match in the north east also included an important 46 not out with the bat. Though he was eventually left stranded, he batted responsibly, hitting only one four in his first 43 deliveries, to make sure England's innings was extended from 211-7 in the 39th over to 265 in the penultimate. "I came in and found it really difficult to start off," he said. "I just re-evaluated what I thought was a good score and obviously what then happened with wickets falling around me a change of the role, just try and bat out the overs." For so long "batting out the overs" has not been the England way, but Jacks is a player growing in maturity. He is also vice-captain to Harry Brook for these Sri Lanka series in the absence of Jacob Bethell and has become an increasingly vocal member of the group. It was telling that when England's T20 World Cup campaign began earlier this year amid the cloud of Brook's Wellington episode, Jacks was first put up to speak to the media. "He's just a good leader," Brook said, plainly. Reliable off the field, Jacks is becoming increasingly so on it. It is 18 months since he moved from the top of the order to the middle as England's finisher in T20 and 50-over cricket. After obvious success as England's player of the tournament at the T20 World Cup in India and Sri Lanka, this was another sign of his growing confidence and ability to do what is needed. Finishers rarely arrive in ideal situations, but their impact can often be match-defining. "I feel very comfortable going out there on the day and any situation can arise which I really enjoy," Jacks said. "It is not the same every day which you get opening so it keeps that fresh element to the game. "At the beginning of my career it felt like you are just fighting to play in the next game, which is not the best place to be. "It is a luxury to know, say when we go to Headingley [for the second ODI], that I will be in the team. You can't take that for granted and appreciate the hard work you have done to get there." It is also easy to forget Jacks began the year in England's Test side, as their spinning all-rounder during the Ashes - a role now filled by Dan Lawrence. Jacks, who met new Test coach Stephen Fleming when the New Zealander joined the white-ball squad at Old Trafford last weekend, has is signed up for a stint with MI Cape Town in the SA20 this winter. There would no clash there with Fleming's first tour in charge in South Africa over Christmas, but the later part of the T20 competition overlaps with England's two Tests in Bangladesh, where English spinners will be needed. "I don't know about what would happen or even if they would want me," he said. "We will finish the summer before getting into the winter." For now, Jacks will focus on white-ball trips to Pakistan, Australia and South Africa as England build towards the 50-over World Cup next autumn. One downside of a Test recall would be losing more time to rearrange that Edinburgh trip. "It didn't go how we planned but we will have to find time to redo it," Jacks smiled. title: Racist message to England footballer Jess Carter denied by teen
description: A court hears that Aaryan Aggarwal called Jess Carter "stupid" and "ugly before using a racial slur.
body: Jess Carter was representing England at the Women's Euro 2025 tournament when the message was sent to her A teenager has denied sending a racist message to England defender Jess Carter on Instagram. Aaryan Aggarwal, 19, allegedly used a racial slur after calling the footballer "stupid" and "ugly" on 17 July 2025. Carter was playing in England's quarter-final at the Women's Euro 2025 tournament when the message was sent, Chelmsford Magistrates' Court heard. Aggarwal, of Dickens Rise in Chigwell, Essex, pleaded not guilty to sending a public communication that was offensive, indecent, obscene or menacing and will stand trial in March. The defendant was arrested in September in connection with the police investigation. "This was an incident on the 17 July 2025. The England footballer Jess Carter was currently playing in the Euro 2025 tournament," said prosecutor Grace Court. "Following a game against Sweden, she received a message." Court said the message read "well done, stupid ugly" - before using a racial slur. Carter joined Gotham FC in the US after a long stint at Chelsea Deputy district judge Christopher Maynard said Aggarwal's trial would take place at Cambridge Magistrates' Court on 3 March. He released Aggarwal on bail, on the condition he did not contact Carter or post about her online. "If you breach that condition or fail to turn up to court when you're required to do so, it's likely you'll be arrested and brought into custody," Maynard warned him. Carter, from Warwick, spent six years at Chelsea FC Women before moving to US-based side Gotham FC in 2024. The 28-year-old was part of the England squad who won their first major women's tournament at Euro 2022. Do you have a story suggestion for Essex? Contact us below. title: Concerns county will not benefit from £2 bus cap
description: Councillor Justine Peberdy says Yeomans Travel and Sargeants Brothers have not committed to the cap.
body: Andy Burnham announced the bus fare cap in England would revert to £2 from January, but there are concerns it will not be implemented in Herefordshire Herefordshire's two largest bus operators have not yet committed to the flat £2 fare being urged by the government, according to council bosses. Ledbury councillor Justine Peberdy said the price cap scheme "will not benefit Herefordshire unless our operators choose to participate in it". Yeomans Travel and Sargeants Brothers, who between them operate a majority of the county's services, did not participate in the current £3 bus fare and there were concerns they would not participate in the new scheme, she said. Yeomans has said it was waiting for more information before deciding. The bus fare cap in England will revert to £2, from the current £3 from January. Peberdy, who chairs a group which looks into how the county's bus services can be improved, confirmed Bromyard-based DRM did plan to participate. Independent councillor Nick Mason said it would be "horrendous" if the rest of the country took part but fares in Herefordshire cost more. Tammy Gerber of local campaign group Buses4Us said the difference between capped and uncapped fares could run to £1,200 a year for someone commuting five days a week in the county. "Herefordshire's operators need to get with the programme before January 2027 and not leave young people to find out the hard way that they've been left behind," she said. Sergeants currently has 24 routes listed on the Herefordshire Council website, chiefly in and around Hereford and westwards towards and into Wales. Yeomans Travel meanwhile operates 31 routes including many serving villages around Hereford, to Leominster and the north and also the southwest of the county. A Yeomans spokesperson said that with the details of the scheme "still evolving", the support on offer from the government would depend on data it had yet to submit. "Consequently, a final decision on participation cannot be made at this point," they said, adding: "We do not expect to receive the government's proposal until late November." Sargeants was also contacted for comment. title: Off sick? You need to phone your boss, back-to-work adviser says
description: Relying on text and email means sick workers disengaged and were less likely to work again, says Sir Charlie Mayfield.
body: People off sick from work should keep in phone contact with their boss, government-appointed back-to-work expert Sir Charlie Mayfield has said. Getting bosses and workers to have a conversation, rather than simply exchanging emails and sicknotes, could help get people back into work, Sir Charlie, who is leading the Keep Britain Working taskforce, said. His latest report said health-related economic inactivity was costing Britain around £210bn a year in benefit payments and lost output. Talking on the phone was just "one piece of the jigsaw" he said on Wednesday. The report calls for more workplace support, external for people with health conditions and disabilities and the establishment of a Workplace Health System alongside the NHS. But improving communication was also a way to "rehumanise" the workplace and help prevent people dropping out of work altogether, Sir Charlie said. Why calling in sick makes you feel guilty The report does not suggest that someone struck down by flu needs to croak through their symptoms over the phone or that bosses need to provide down-the-line sickbed sympathy if an employee is off with food poisoning. "I'm not worried about a day here and a day there. It is more about longer term issues," Sir Charlie told the BBC's Today Programme. But he said Britain was doing a "poor job" of handling sickness in the workplace, leading to more people becoming disengaged and dropping out altogether. "I have met so many people who have said to me, 'You know, I was signed off sick and I was off sick for a month, two months, three months, and I had almost no contact with my employer'," Sir Charlie said. Around 300,000 people leave work every year with a health condition, much of which is preventable, the report said. Sir Charlie said employees sometimes feared talking about long-term health issues with their employer. "But the fear is also felt by employers as well because they're afraid of causing offence or creating a complaint or a grievance," he added. Fear on both sides can create a distance and lack of understanding, he warned, with longer absences making it much more likely a worker will drop out of the labour force altogether. "If you can keep more people in work, there's a massive opportunity for us to add billions to the economy and, frankly, to people's livelihoods," Sir Charlie said. "To get that, though, you need to have people talking to each other, and you've got to more actively manage sickness and ill health in the workplace." Employers need to do more, he said, and employees need to engage with it. Other ways for bosses to support staff include ensuring access to treatments such as physiotherapy and talking therapies, he said. Have you been affected by issues covered in this story? title: Inmates deny attempt to murder Sara Sharif's father
description: Steven Sansom and Adam Watson pleaded not guilty to trying to kill Urfan Sharif in a prison attack.
body: Urfan Sharif was jailed for life for the murder of his daughter at their home in Woking Two prisoners have pleaded not guilty to the attempted murder of Urfan Sharif, who is serving a life sentence for killing his 10-year-old daughter, Sara Sharif. Steven Sansom, 47, and Adam Watson, 39, were charged last month following an attack in Belmarsh Prison on 1 January 2025, which reportedly left Sharif with cuts to his face. Sharif and Sara's stepmother, Beinash Batool, were sentenced to life imprisonment for murdering Sara at their home in Woking, Surrey. Sansom and Watson appeared at the Old Bailey via video links from HMP Wakefield on Wednesday. The hearing was told how Samsom reportedly invited Sharif into a cell at Belmarsh, where Watson was waiting, at which point Watson allegedly took hold of him and punched him repeatedly before Sansom applied pressure to his throat. Prosecutors then claim Watson passed an object to Sansom, which was used to make cutting motions to Sharif's throat. The pair also deny wounding with intent to cause grievous bodily harm, and unauthorised possession of two weapons in the form of a tin lid, and a pen attached to a handle. Sara Sharif was killed in 2023 Judge Lynn Tayton KC set a two-week trial for 19 July, 2027, with pre-trial hearing set for June. Urfan Sharif was sentenced to a minimum of 40 years in prison for murder, while his wife Beinash Batool, 30, received a minimum of 33 years. Sara's uncle, Faisal Malik, 29, was sentenced to 16 years' imprisonment for causing or allowing her death. The three fled to Pakistan, with Sara's five siblings, the day before her body was found in 2023. They hid out there for four weeks before returning to the UK, where they were arrested. Sara's siblings remain in Pakistan, where they have been living with their paternal grandfather. Additional reporting by PA Media. title: Trump meets US-backed Venezuelan president for first time since Maduro seized
description: Rodriguez was handpicked by Trump as leader of Venezuela was arrested and taken to the US
body: Delcy Rodríguez was pictured alongside the US president on the sidelines of the summit in New York US President Donald Trump has held talks with Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodríguez at the UN General Assembly, their first face-to-face meeting since the White House backed her to take over the South American country's government. Rodríguez succeeded Nicolás Maduro shortly after US forces conducted a raid on the Venezuelan capital Caracas and seized him. The pair met a few kilometres from the New York jail where Maduro is awaiting trial for drug trafficking and other charges. Rodríguez said they discussed "advancing a cooperation agenda in strategic areas such as energy, mining, and security". US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles also attended the meeting. Rodríguez's government has signed an agreement allowing the US to control more than 65 billion barrels of its oil - more than a fifth of the country's reserves. It grants a US-led company 100-year concessions over 17 oilfields in Venezuela. Trump previously called it "the biggest oil deal in world history". During his address to the UN on Monday, Trump said the US and Venezuela control "more than 60%" of the world's oil, adding: "To the victor belong the spoils." Rodríguez is due to address the UN on Wednesday. She previously served as vice-president to Maduro and was sanctioned by the US in 2018, but the measures were lifted in April this year. She was sworn in as interim president by Venezuela's National Assembly days after the US raid with the White House's blessing. Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado has repeatedly been barred from re-entering the country. title: Drug deaths in Scotland rise 11% as country struggles with worst rate in Europe
description: The figure rose by 11% last year, bringing the total deaths in a decade to more than 11,000.
body: Deaths related to illicit drugs rose by 11% in Scotland last year to 1,133 as the country struggles to tackle the worst fatality rate in Europe. National Records of Scotland (NRS) said the figure for 2025 was 116 higher than the previous year, bringing the total deaths in a decade to more than 11,000. After adjusting for age, there were 214 drug-related deaths per million people. NRS defines drug-related deaths as those where the underlying cause was drug poisoning, a controlled substance was in the body at the time of death, and drug use led directly to the death. Efforts to save lives over the past year have been hampered by criminal gangs mixing powerful synthetic opioids such as nitazenes with existing drugs including heroin, cocaine and fake Valium pills. Nitazenes were implicated in 247 deaths in 2025 - more than 22% of the total. The figure had more than trebled from 76 deaths the previous year. Opiates and opioids, such as heroin, continued to be the most common type of drug implicated in deaths, accounting for 78% of the total. Cocaine was implicated in 52% of deaths, the highest figure since NRS began publishing specific data in 2008. NRS said the increase had been driven by a rise in deaths of male drug users. This increased by 19%, while the rate of female deaths fell by 5%. The rate of drug-related deaths in the most deprived areas of Scotland was 15 times as high as in the least deprived areas. The average age of death has increased from 32 in 2000 to 46 years in 2025. Over a five year period from 2021-25, Glasgow recorded the highest average death rate at 380 per million, followed by 340 per million in Dundee and 310 per million in North Ayrshire. When comparing Scotland with the rest of Europe, NRS measures the death rate among 15-64 year olds - which was 277 per million in 2025. The next highest rate in Europe was Estonia with 112 deaths per million in 2024, the most recent year for which figures are available from the European Union Drugs Agency (EUDA). Scotland's death rate in 2024 was 246 per million. NRS says its methodology produces "similar" outcomes to EUDA's count of "drug-induced deaths", with the caveat that the two methods use slightly different lists of drugs. When comparing Scotland with the rest of the UK, NRS uses a wider measure of age-adjusted drug poisoning deaths. This includes all deaths where the underlying cause was listed as mental and behavioural disorders due to psychoactive substance abuse or poisoning by drugs whether accidental, intentional, of unknown intent or as a result of assault. The most recent comparable data are for 2024 and show that Scotland had an age-adjusted death rate of 216 per million compared with 91 for England, 140 for Wales and 135 for Northern Ireland. title: Farmers' fury at online scramble for £233m funding
description: Farmers fear they may not be able to carry out environmental work because they lost out on funding.
body: Many farmers rely on government payments to manage their land in more environmentally-friendly ways Thousands of farmers missed out on vital government funding after online applications for a £233m green scheme for the whole of England closed down in under six hours. Farming and environmental groups condemned the race to secure the sustainable farming incentive (SFI) funding, with some comparing it to a "frantic" online scramble to secure Glastonbury or Oasis gig tickets. The post-Brexit scheme, which replaced EU subsidies with payments for farmers to look after nature and provide "public goods", opened at 10:00 BST on Tuesday but had run out of budget by 15:48 BST. The government said farmers had responded "in force" to the scheme and there would be further funding opportunities for 2027. The SFI scheme had been shut without warning last year so demand from farmers was expected to be high The National Farmers' Union (NFU) is calling for the government to explain why the scheme opened and closed so quickly, with so many farmers left out of pocket. It said it wanted "clarity and urgency" from the government and added that it had made "repeated warnings of a lack of sufficient budget". NFU vice-president Robyn Munt said: "The rapid uptake of the scheme comes as no surprise. We have made the demand clear to Defra for some time. "Its closure in less than six hours shows the scale of demand there is from farmers to deliver for the environment and to invest in farm resilience." Vicki Hird, agriculture lead at the Wildlife Trusts said "the scramble for green farming schemes was worse than the dash for Oasis tickets". She added: "The budget has been inadequate for far too long and the Treasury must recognise this and allocate far greater funds to ensure climate resilience in farming in the next budget." The SFI scheme is vital for many farmers who have turned large swathes of their land over to nature-friendly schemes, such as planting hedges, creating wildflower margins and protecting the soil. When the scheme was suddenly closed without notice last year, there were concerns that some farmers might turn their backs on environmental work if they could not access the payments and demand for Tuesday's scheme was expected to be high. The Nature Friendly Farming Network (NFFN), which helps farmers to manage land in environmentally-friendly ways, criticised the "frantic scramble" and said farmers had "faced a desperate race against time" to secure their funding agreements. Cambridgeshire arable farmer Martin Lines, who leads the NFFN, said: "This entire SFI system, with windows opening and closing within a few hours, isn't fit for purpose. "We need to find a better way based on continuous, whole-farm agreements, not doors that slam shut on day one because the money has already gone." He pointed out that after years of extreme weather, many farmers were relying on the funding to help adapt their farms to climate change and become more resilient. The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said it would provide further information on future opportunities for funding applications in 2027 "soon". A Defra spokesperson said: "This year we ensured small farms and those new to SFI were prioritised - with an exclusive first window in the summer. "In anticipation of high demand in the second window, ministers decided to allocate an additional £20m to the fund, on top the £50m announced by the prime minister in August, so that we could fund as many agreements as possible." Farming Minister Stephen Morgan added that the SFI had been designed to be simpler to apply for and that farmers had "responded in force". "This is a scheme that works for farmers, backs food production, and delivers practical, sustainable land management, supporting the aims of our farming roadmap, our long-term plan for English farming," he said. title: Neighbours 'broken' over family's house fire deaths
description: An injured man, who was found outside the house in Bootle, remains in hospital, police say.
body: Tributes, including flowers and teddy bears, have been laid at the scene Neighbours of a mother and three children killed in a house fire have said their community has been "broken" by their deaths. The fire at the house on Stone Square in Bootle, Merseyside, "spread rapidly" in the early hours of Tuesday morning. An injured man who was outside the house when fire crews arrived remains in hospital. Cards addressed to the family, as well as teddy bears and photographs, have been left close to the scene by bereaved relatives and shocked locals. Loti Nambobe, who is taking care of the family's dog after the fire, said: "It's a community. It's broken. It hurts." A joint investigation involving Merseyside Police and Merseyside Fire and Rescue Service is expected to continue into this afternoon, with a mobile incident room set up close to the scene in the hours after the fire. The Bishop of Liverpool the Rt Rev Ruth Worsley and Bishop of Warrington the Rt Rev Simon Robinson said they were "deeply saddened to hear of the devastating incident". "Our thoughts and prayers are with their families and loved ones at this unimaginably difficult time," they added. Bootle MP Peter Dowd said: "My heart goes out to the family and friends of the four who lost their lives in a house fire in Bootle. "Their loss is beyond words. This shocking event will touch everyone in our community." Chief fire officer Nick Searle said the "intense fire" spread rapidly Dowd said that police and other emergency services "must be allowed to undertake their investigations into this tragic situation". "I also want to put on record the outstanding work our emergency services do in such challenging personal circumstances," he added. Merseyside Fire and Rescue Service (MFRS) arrived on the scene at about 03:40 BST on Tuesday and found the semi-detached house "well alight". A man, understood to have also lived in the house, was found badly burned outside and was taken to hospital. Fire crews went into the house to try to bring the blaze under control and search for anyone inside. MFRS later confirmed that four people "showing no signs of life" had been found in an upstairs bedroom. Nambombe said before the fire crews arrived, neighbours had been attempting to get into the house to try to rescue the family trapped inside. "There were guys that tried to go in. People were doing everything, honestly," he said. "Like everyone here is a family and it's broken everyone." A neighbour, who asked not to be named, told the BBC: "They were good people, just a normal family getting on with life… who loved their kids." A police van remains at the scene at the cordon of the cul-de-sac. Dozens of tributes including cards, flowers, candles, teddy bears and pink and blue star-shaped balloons have been laid on the pavement next to the cordon. Kevin Longshaw, area manager for MFRS, described it as a devastating incident, and said thoughts were very much with the family and friends of those who had lost their lives and been injured. He said they would work closely with relevant colleagues to determine the cause of the fire. title: Ofcom launches investigation into Pornhub over its age checks
description: The regulator said it had concerns Aylo "may not have conducted sufficient due diligence" over verifying the age of its users.
body: Ofcom has launched an investigation into Pornhub owner, Aylo, over whether the site's new age checks are effectively stopping children from accessing adult content. The regulator said in May that Pornhub started using a new age verification process for some users, which relies on a third party, in this case Apple. It said it had concerns that Aylo "may not have conducted sufficient due diligence and testing" before implementing this new process, and so it "may not be highly effective" at preventing children from seeing pornography. Under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA), sites that host pornographic material must use highly effective age assurance to ensure whether a user is over 18. The BBC has approached Aylo for comment. Ofcom says as part of its investigation it will consider how Aylo implements its age verification processes and whether it conducted the "necessary due diligence" before it was implemented. It will not investigate how Apple operates its age checks. George Lusty, Ofcom's Director of Enforcement, said: "Online age checks are a vital protection to prevent children from encountering inappropriate or harmful material, including pornography. "We expect tech firms to ensure age checks are highly effective before introducing them. Anything less could leave children at risk." Under the Online Safety Act, Ofcom holds the power to fine non-compliant companies up to £18 million or 10% of their annual global turnover, whichever is greater. This probe is just the latest clash between the regulator and what is one of the world's most viewed porn sites. In January, Pornhub announced it would restrict access to its website in the UK blaming the tougher age checks introduced as part of the OSA. Aylo said that updates to the Act requiring age verification had "not achieved its goal of protecting minors" and had "diverted traffic to darker, unregulated corners of the internet". However, in May, it said it would be making the site available again for some UK Apple users who had confirmed their age with the company's most up-to-date version of iOS, its mobile operating system. title: UK economy will grow by less than expected next year, OECD says
description: Higher energy prices due to the conflict in the Middle East and climate change could hit growth.
body: The UK will grow by less than expected next year amid the ongoing US-Israel war in Iran, an international agency has said. It is one of many countries whose economic prospects are facing a hit due to the prolonged conflict, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) said. The downgrade to the UK's economic growth outlook is moderate, according to the OECD, which predicted it will grow by 1% in 2027, against an earlier forecast of 1.1%. The agency also upgraded the UK's growth outlook for 2026, from an expected 0.9% to 1.1% for the year. The prediction comes as Chancellor John Healey prepares to deliver his first Budget at the end of October. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has made easing the cost of living for household one of his key aims, while the government is under pressure to spend more on defence. However, Burnham and Healey face a difficult balancing act, trying to offer more support to households while sticking to Labour's manifesto commitments on tax and the government's self-imposed fiscal rules. Inflation has also pushed up the cost of interest on government debt, which alongside an unexpected surge in government borrowing in August has added to the pressure on Healey. In the short-term, UK growth in 2026 is expected to be higher than the OECD predicted in June after "solid domestic demand growth". But it will be lower than predicted in 2027 as higher fuel prices eat into growth. The effects of this depend on how long supply disruptions last, it said. Risks to the global economy include the war in the Middle East and climate-change related supply shocks, the OECD said. Next year, global growth is expected to also be 0.1% lower, with countries affected including Australia, Canada, and the Euro-area. Conflict in the Middle East has contributed to higher oil and gas prices globally, pushing up inflation in countries including the UK. Weather-related shocks, including from a strong El Nino, could hit farmers and help push up food prices, it added. title: Nigella Lawson is 'icing on the cake', TV critics say as she enters Bake Off tent
description: The TV chef joined Paul Hollywood in the tent as the Channel 4 competition returned for a new series.
body: Nigella has taken over from Prue Leith as a judge on Bake Off alongside Paul Hollywood TV critics have described Nigella Lawson as the "icing on the cake" of The Great British Bake Off, after the show returned for a new series on Tuesday. Lawson has replaced Dame Prue Leith, who announced she was leaving earlier this year after nearly a decade in the programme's famous tent. The Telegraph said Lawson gives the Channel 4 series a "new lease of life", while Digital Spy agreed she was a "brilliant addition" to the line-up. But the Independent was cooler on the launch episode as a whole, saying the show "wastes Nigella's prodigious charms and misses chance for a true revamp". The return of Bake Off saw Lawson join fellow judge Paul Hollywood, who has appeared on the programme since its launch in 2010, and presenters Alison Hammond and Noel Fielding. Former Bake Off winner Giuseppe Dell'Anno told BBC Radio 4's Today that Lawson "did produce a step change" to the show and was a "nice fit with the ethos of the programme". "She was doing her best by capturing the vibes of a cake, the feelings, what it makes you think of, which was very nicely balanced by Paul being very technical and scrutinising," he said. "I think, however, that she will get better over time, because my gut feeling yesterday was that she was still in new territory." Some critics noted Lawson did not deliver as much innuendo as expected during her first episode In a five-star review, the Guardian's Lucy Mangan, external said Lawson "moves through Bake Off dispensing words of wisdom, generous praise and gentle criticism". She added that Lawson is "just as confident as Leith but a much quieter, more soothing presence that works perfectly with Alison Hammond's ebullience and Paul Hollywood's teacher-ish vibe". The Telegraph's Anita Singh, external also awarded five stars, remarking that "Bake Off and Nigella are a match made in heaven". "She brings glamour, intelligence and poise. And, of course, a hefty dollop of innuendo," Singh said. "Lawson is supportive in her judging but not afraid to tell the bakers where they can improve. She gives helpful advice." The launch episode was described as "one of the most disastrous openers ever" by Metro's Adam Miller, external - but luckily he was only referring to the cakes. "When Bake Off should be crumbling after 17 seasons, Nigella Lawson is making Channel 4's crown jewel fresher than ever," he said. "It's clear to see she is the lifeline Bake Off needed to ensure it could easily have another decade or more in it yet." However, other critics said Channel 4 had missed an opportunity to revitalise the programme. Awarding two stars, the Independent's Nick Hilton, external said Lawson quickly "feels part of the fabric". "But this is also the problem," he continued. "The Bake Off format is very tired. The cakes wobble, the decorations melt, the bakers over-salt the batter, and everything remains the same. "Nigella's arrival might have been an opportunity for a harder refresh. But instead of bending the format to suit Nigella, the new judge bends to the will of the programme." Hilton acknowledged that producers "might have done brilliantly to snag Nigella, and it will undoubtedly lead to an uptick in viewers". "But they've applied her prodigious charms too thinly, and even she – with her preference for all things 'sumptuous' – can't stop the feeling that the show has gone more than a little stale." Several critics noted that Lawson did not deliver as much innuendo as expected during her debut in the tent. "Add Nigella – famous for her on-screen coquettish eyelash-fluttering and cheeky language choices – into the mix, and you'd imagine the sauciness gets dialled up to 11," said the Radio Times's Jane Rackham, external. "Instead, she's cut back on the sauce. She makes well-informed and helpful comments about the amateur bakers' efforts." Digital Spy's Janet A Leigh agreed, external, noting: "As is the nature of Bake Off, there were many opportunities for Nigella to engage with the playful, flirtatious nature that has underpinned the show since its inception. Yet every opportunity was gently rebuffed." Instead, she said, Lawson "has a way of talking about food that celebrates it and expands the audience's understanding of flavours without seeming pretentious. "If episode one is just a flavour of what to expect from Nigella, then it is hugely encouraging. She cares deeply, steers wisely, and slots effortlessly into the close-knit team." When Lawson was faced with innuendo-laden comments from contestants or co-stars, she often "wisely said nothing", noted the Daily Mail's Jan Moir., external "Ultimately this was a tremendous debut performance from the new mistress of meringue, showing a side of Nigella we have not seen before: quirky, commanding, funny – but also humane," she concluded. Ben Dowell of the Times observed, external: "Bake Off has always been one of TV's more beguiling offerings with a comforting romance about it. "It's not perfect. Hammond is ebullience and warmth personified but her co-presenter, the erstwhile Mighty Boosh comedian Fielding, still looks a bit lost, as if he has wandered in from the wrong set. "But with Nigella the show is definitely in safe hands. Bake Off has found a new star." title: Prince and Princess of Wales share a laugh with Tom Cruise at film premiere
description: William and Catherine renew their friendship with the Hollywood star at the premiere for his film Digger.
body: The Prince and Princess of Wales renewed their friendship with Tom Cruise at the premiere of the Hollywood star's latest film in London on Tuesday. Cruise took the hand of Catherine, Princess of Wales, as they talked and laughed on a black carpet - instead of the traditional red - before the royal gala screening of Digger in Leicester Square. Cruise has known the prince and princess for a number of years and also met William's mother, Princess Diana, and attended her funeral in 1997. Catherine wore a pair of Diana's pearl drop earrings to the premiere on Tuesday, as well as the late Queen Mother's amethyst sautoir necklace. Cruise complimented Prince William on his "great jacket", referring to the prince's black velvet jacket. Catherine wore a purple, floor-length Jenny Packham dress. David Beckham was among the other big names at the premiere, along with his sons Cruz and Romeo. Digger sees Cruise transformed into a grey-haired oil baron who has to clean up his environmental mess, and is directed by Oscar winner Alejandro González Iñárritu. Full reviews have not yet been published, but critics' reactions on social media have been mixed. IndieWire's Anne Thompson described it as "a brave and gorgeous art film that will not score with mainstream audiences but will play best for the Academy" - referring to the Oscars voters. But Awards Radar editor Joey Magidson said it is "a mess" and "wasn't enjoyable". The film will be released in the UK and US on 2 October. title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC
description: Defence Secretary Wes Streeting has confirmed the review after Donald Trump told Andy Burnham the deal was "terrible".
body: A strategic military base is located on the Chagos archipelago's largest island, Diego Garcia The UK is reviewing its deal to hand over the Chagos Islands to Mauritius, the defence secretary has said. Wes Streeting confirmed the deal was being looked at again after US President Donald Trump called it "terrible" at the UN General Assembly on Tuesday. The original agreement would see the UK cede sovereignty of the territory to Mauritius and pay an average of £101m ($136m) per year to lease back a joint UK-US military base there, prized for its strategic location in the Indian Ocean. In April the deal, agreed under Sir Keir Starmer, was paused indefinitely because Trump pulled his support. Streeting said "we have to" review the deal "because the United States doesn't support it". "What President Trump said yesterday wasn't new but I think it does provide absolute clarity that his position on this Chagos deal as currently drafted is not changing," he told BBC Breakfast. "So we have to do more work with our American allies, with President Trump and his administration, to get the deal to a place where he can support it." Streeting said the focus now would be to secure a long-term certainty for the base on Diego Garcia, the Chagos archipelago's largest island. He said it had been the view of every UK prime minister since Boris Johnson that an ongoing legal process - as Mauritius argues it was illegally forced to give away the islands in 1965 to gain independence - risks the security of the base. During Trump's first face-to-face meeting with Prime Minister Andy Burnham at the UN General Assembly in New York, the US president criticised the "terrible deal" and said the UK was "going to be looking" at it. He later told broadcasters he has "inherited the situation and we need a resolution". Burnham added: "It's critical to safeguard the future of the base, and that matters to us for security reasons, but also clearly to the United States as well. "What I said in the meeting is that we will work to find that resolution between the different sides, and we'll work hard to find it." The prime minister had spoken to his Mauritian counterpart, Navin Ramgoolam, ahead of his trip to New York. An official readout from that meeting said Burnham "reiterated his commitment to continue doing everything possible" along with the US to ratify the deal. Prior to the pause in April, the UK and Mauritius had signed an agreement in May 2025 but a final draft of the bill to hand over sovereignty of the islands had not passed Parliament. Under the terms of the deal agreed in 2025, Britain would hand sovereignty over the Indian Ocean archipelago to Mauritius but lease back the Diego Garcia base for 99 years, with official figures giving the total as £3.4bn. However, Sir Keir, who was then prime minister, came under heavy criticism from opponents who said the real cost of the deal could amount to about £35bn, adjusting for inflation, and risked allowing China to establish a presence on the archipelago. Trump has been a frequent critic of the deal, previously branding it a "a blight on our great ally" and an "act of total weakness". Reacting to the review, Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch called on Burnham to "just scrap this terrible deal". Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said: "The Chagos deal is dead. Thank God." Streeting told BBC Radio 4's Today programme on Wednesday that no money would be handed over to Mauritius "at this stage" while officials review the deal. Describing the Diego Garcia base as "one of the most sensitive and valuable national security assets", he said work was underway to find a deal "that maybe not everyone loves, but everyone can live with". title: Hadjar to stay as Verstappen's Red Bull team-mate for 2027
description: Frenchman Isack Hadjar is to stay at Red Bull as Max Verstappen's team-mate for the 2027 season.
body: Isack Hadjar will drive at this weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix after missing three races because of a wrist injury Frenchman Isack Hadjar is to stay at Red Bull as Max Verstappen's team-mate for the 2027 season. The 21-year-old was promoted to the senior team this season after a rookie year with Racing Bulls and has managed to be closer to Verstappen on pace than any team-mate since Daniel Ricciardo in 2018. His best result this season came with a third place at the Monaco Grand Prix. Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies described the move as "an easy decision". Mekies said: "Since joining us at the start of the year, Isack has been superb on and off track, especially considering this is only his second F1 season." Hadjar returns to Red Bull for this weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix after missing the past three races with a broken wrist, an injury sustained while boxing as part of his training programme. Mekies added: "You could see from his first weekend in Melbourne that he handled the step up with remarkable composure and had earned his place in this seat. "The period since his injury has been a difficult one for Isack, but this extension shows how much we believe in him." Hadjar said: "I came to this team eight months ago and immediately understood the scale and ambition of this organisation. "There are so many talented people at the factory, and you're aware of the privilege of driving for such an incredible team alongside a four-time world champion like Max. "I'm constantly looking to listen, learn and push myself further every single day, which only makes me more excited about what lies ahead." Over the first half of the season, Hadjar was 0.239 seconds slower than Verstappen on average in qualifying and has managed to out-qualify the Dutchman three times, in Australia, Japan and Britain. In Silverstone Verstappen had a down-on-power engine and in Australia the Dutchman crashed at the start of qualifying. Verstappen signed a two-year extension to his contract, that now runs to the end of 2030, in August. title: Eleven killed in mass shooting at house in South Africa
description: One of those killed is believed to be a pregnant woman, police said.
body: South Africa has one of the world's highest murder rates At least 11 people have been killed in a mass shooting in a residential building near the South African city of Durban. Gunmen stormed a house in the KwaMakhutha township late on Tuesday and opened fire on 14 people. Ten were killed at the scene and four were taken to hospital, where one later died from their injuries, police said. Police said some of the victims were on their watch in connection with illegal activities, which they could not "divulge at the moment to protect investigations which have been launched". While the motive of the shooting has not yet confirmed, the police said they could not rule out a "feud between rival groupings". "Information available at this stage suggests that 13 men and one woman, who is believed to be pregnant, were reportedly having a party inside a house when three men arrived and opened fire on them," the police said in a statement. The woman is among those who died. A local TV reporter from the eNCA channel at the scene said the gunmen had set fire to a vehicle belonging to one of the victims before fleeing, with footage showing the burnt-out car. The police say they have launched a manhunt for the suspects. South Africa has one of the world's highest murder rates, with police data showing a murder rate equivalent to more than 60 deaths a day. In recent weeks, the gruesome discovery of at least nine murdered women, with some of the bodies dumped by the roadside, has heightened fears in the country. Last year, nine people were killed in a mass shooting at a tavern in Johannesburg. Rivalry among criminal gangs amid turf wars, drug trafficking and illegal mining is common in the country, often driving violence within communities. In February, President Cyril Ramaphosa said organised crime was "the most immediate threat to our democracy, our society and our economic development", as he announced that he would be deploying the army to support the police. title: Germany's saviour? How Klopp is looking to turn fortunes around
description: As Jurgen Klopp prepares for his first game as Germany manager, BBC Sport looks at how is trying to turn their fortunes around.
body: Jurgen Klopp has picked a split squad for Germany's opening Nations League games It has been quite the ride since Jurgen Klopp was announced as Germany's head coach in July. In his first news conference, Klopp admonished the media, urging them to treat him fairly and refrain from any attacks against his family. Last Thursday, during another media conference, Klopp called for "positive patriotism" amid political turmoil in the country. When asked whether he considers himself an ambassador for Germany in his new role, Klopp's answer was a serious one. "From my perspective as a sportsman, I can say that I would very much like to reclaim the flag for myself, for all of us," said Klopp. "I want it so that when someone waves it, no-one thinks: 'What is wrong with you?' Instead, I want people to understand: You are happy and realise how lucky you were to be born, grow up, or move to this wonderful country." His statement was made in light of the success of the Alternative for Germany (AfD) in the state election in Saxony-Anhalt. The anti-immigration party has since scored another win in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. Klopp's remarks were widely and positively discussed in the media - the German national team represents a diverse Germany, as several players come from a migrant background. KIopp also remarked about the recent success of Alexander Zverev at the US Open, the women's basketball team at the European Championship and German athletes at the European Athletics Championships, saying sport can ensure "a sense of community". He added: "This is our mission: we need to create a good atmosphere." Klopp knows, intentionally or not, how to make headlines. However, the German Football Association (DFB) didn't hire the former Liverpool boss on an annual salary of £6m to become a commentator on the state of Germany - but to transform a floundering national team. Klopp wants to 'reclaim' flag amid German elections Klopp starts Germany reign by threatening to quit Between the two news conferences, Klopp looked like the busiest national team boss on the planet, making countless visits to league games and training facilities. One day fans could see Klopp sitting in the stands of Dortmund's Signal Iduna Park, his old stomping ground and, not long after, they may have caught a picture of him in the VIP lounge of Mainz's stadium or somewhere near Eintracht Frankfurt's training pitch talking to players. Klopp has approached this new job with open eyes. Initially, the charismatic 59-year-old drew up a list of 57 players who could have been selected for this first international break. "Players will receive chances who don't even expect it yet," Klopp said in July. His first selection wasn't short of surprises. In the flavour of a trial-and-error principle, Klopp and his staff decided to select two almost completely different squads for the upcoming four games. The first squad, including Joshua Kimmich, Kai Havertz and Jamal Musiala, will face arch-rivals the Netherlands at Johan Cruyff Arena on Thursday (19:45 BST) and host Greece on Sunday. The second squad, with Florian Wirtz and Aleksandar Pavlovic, face Serbia at home and Greece on the road in the second half of this international break. The only player who was selected for both is back-up goalkeeper Finn Dahmen. The selection process means we will not see Germany's best starting XI this time around. Instead, Klopp clearly intends to try out new players, some of whom played in Germany's second tier only a few months ago. Take, for example, Felix Keidel, a 23-year-old full-back-midfielder hybrid from recently promoted SV Elversberg. A year ago, Keidel was as far away from the national team as the Oktoberfest from Rio Carnival. Now Keidel - just like Mika Baur, Bambase Conte, Max Rosenfelder, Philipp Treu, and Vitaly Janelt - has the chance to show he could be a valuable cog in the machine. Klopp has never built his success merely on star names - he has always taken a liking to undervalued and overlooked players. He once signed an little-known Polish winger by the name of Lukasz Piszczek and moulded him into one of the best right-backs in Europe who would go toe-to-toe with Cristiano Ronaldo in his prime. And he helped transform Andy Robertson into a force on Liverpool's left side. Klopp's style helps to elevate all the members of his squad - not just the most talented. Fitness and mental readiness are highly important, and some newcomers might just have that to impress the new manager. But man-marking is prevalent in Germany's top flight, while Klopp prefers his teams to close down the player in possession to create superior numbers around the ball. So some of the Bundesliga players will have to adapt quickly. "It is not important who plays but how someone plays," Klopp said last week. "I expect a lot from the beginning. It could be a bit wild, but I accept that. It just has to be lively." Klopp has chosen younger squads compared to the ones we saw in the past couple of years. Manuel Neuer, Antonio Rudiger and Pascal Gross have retired from international football, and other 30-somethings might just not receive a chance to get into the team again. "I think it is about time to wish the new generation best of luck," Gross said after Brighton's win over Arsenal on Saturday. "I still enjoy playing football here in the club, but there's a change in Germany and rightfully so." Youth and energy seem to be preferred. "I have the desire to work with guys who cannot wait to wear this jersey, who want to play the kind of football everybody enjoys and who perform even better wearing the national team jersey," Klopp said. title: MLS coach sacked after sexist remark to female referee
description: MLS club Columbus Crew sack their reserve team coach after he refused to let go of a female referee's hand and says "don't forget this is a man's game".
body: Federico Higuain spent eight seasons with Columbus Crew as a player Major League Soccer club Columbus Crew have sacked their reserve team coach after he refused to let go of a female referee's hand and said "don't forget this is a man's game". Federico Higuain, brother of former Real Madrid striker Gonzalo Higuain, was sent off and given a two-match suspension for the incident during an MLS Next Pro league match. "We determined it's in the best interest of our club, players and support staff to dismiss Federico Higuain from his responsibilities," Crew general manager Issa Tall said in a statement. "After conversations this week and further assessing the past month, our club's standards of what's expected from a leader for one of our teams have not been met." Meanwhile, the Professional Soccer Referees Association (PSRA) criticised the league's response, saying Higuain's two-game ban "falls drastically short". A statement from the referees' union added: "A male head coach committed two deliberate acts of physical abuse and sexism against a female official - squeezing her hand and refusing to let go after being told to stop three times. "This physical intimidation was compounded by a demeaning, sexist remark to the official: 'Don't forget, this is a man's game.' "Women make every level of this game better. They should not have to endure intimidation or degrading comments to prove it. "Our female officials have proven their excellence on the world stage. They deserve the same respect, dignity, and safe working environment as every other official." title: Trump administration accuses banned media outlets of 'falsehoods' ahead of court hearing
description: The US Justice Department's response to a lawsuit filed by CNN, Politico and MS NOW also cites national security.
body: A judge will rule on Wednesday whether to lift Donald Trump's ban on CNN, Politico and MS NOW entering the White House The US Justice Department has filed documents that accuse three media outlets banned from the White House of "trafficking in verifiable falsehoods" and reporting which "threatened national security" as it prepared to defend the move in court. Last week, President Donald Trump barred CNN, Politico and MS NOW from the White House, accusing them of spreading "fake news". After their reporters had their passes confiscated and were denied access to the building, the three outlets jointly launched legal action, calling the move unconstitutional. On Wednesday, a judge is set to decide whether to issue an order temporarily lifting the ban, pending a full hearing. According to a court filing by the Justice Department in a District of Columbia court, the three outlets were issued with a list of "reporting incidents" by the White House ahead of the ban. The filing cites a number of stories about construction at the White House - including about a security bunker and the building of a new ballroom, as well as a report on an internal information leak investigation. It goes on to say that "access to the White House is a privilege, not a right". The three media organisations have argued that the ban breaches their rights under the First Amendment, which forbids the government from "abridging" the freedom of the press. In a joint statement confirming legal action against the government, they said: "Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists' credentials because it objected to our reporting. "Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public's right to independent journalism free from government interference." Major TV networks have withdrawn from a media-sharing arrangement of video and images of the president, known as the pool, in protest over the ban. Shortly after, the White House launched its own streaming channel, Trump TV, which operates a 24/7 feed of clips of the president. What is the White House pool and why is it in a row with Trump? title: How Premier League teams have really started - according to xG
description: Which Premier League teams have overperformed their xG and who has underperformed?
body: Which Premier League teams are overperforming their xG? How have Premier League teams really started? At this stage last season Liverpool were top, with five wins out of five, and Tottenham were third. Given that they finished fifth and 17th respectively, it shows that the table shouldn't be taken too seriously this early on. While any statistics should be taken with a pinch of salt - given such a small sample size of games and the fact that some teams have had more difficult starts than others - they do provide a more accurate picture of how the season could unfold. Expected goals (xG) tells us how much teams have dominated games, based on the number and quality of shots they've taken and faced. Basically, how well they've performed in general before finishing, shot-stopping and plain old luck come into play. And Premier League history shows us that the more a team dominates games, the more points they win in the long run. It's best to exclude penalties as refereeing decisions and defensive clumsiness give a false impression of how good teams actually are at attacking and defending, especially at this early stage. Champions Arsenal may have suffered their biggest defeat in three years last weekend at Brighton but they've still been the best team overall based on xG difference. Leaders Manchester City are not too far behind them in terms of how much they've dominated their games, while there's nothing fortunate about unbeaten Brentford's impressive start to the season. Manchester United constantly seem to flip between feast and famine, when often they've simply been fine. Despite their underwhelming start, only three teams have a higher xG difference so far. The likes of Nottingham Forest and Bournemouth have also been better than their position in the early table suggests. At the other end, Aston Villa, Crystal Palace and Newcastle have been the least impressive in terms of their overall performance, with the latter perhaps the most surprising given their position in the top half. It's still early days, so there's no need to panic just yet, but it shows that those teams have a lot of room to improve - something Villa did to great effect after a slow start last season by finishing fourth. Worryingly for the established sides though, the promoted teams seem like they won't be going down without a fight, with both Hull and Ipswich making genuinely solid starts to the campaign. Looking at teams' numbers going forward, Brighton have the best attack so far based on the number and quality of chances they've had, followed by Manchester City, Brentford and Manchester United. Although the Gunners are more admired for their defensive prowess, it's still surprising that eight teams have a higher xG than champions Arsenal, while Liverpool and Chelsea also rank in mid-table. Brighton not only have the highest xG but have also been one of the most ruthless sides in front of goal, scoring 15 non-penalty goals from their 10.7 xG. The only team to be more clinical than the Seagulls is their avian cousins the Magpies, who actually have the lowest xG in the league so far. Newcastle have scored twice as many goals as a team historically would given the chances they've had - 9 goals from 4.5 xG - but head coach Matthias Jaissle will no doubt want his team to create more and not have to rely on such sharp finishing as the season goes on. In contrast, Coventry, Sunderland, Nottingham Forest and Tottenham have all scored three goals fewer than they really should have given the opportunities they've had in their first five games. It'll be interesting to see whether those teams genuinely have a problem with their finishing or if their luck in front of goal simply begins to change in the games to come. As mentioned earlier, champions Arsenal are renowned for their defence and they still have by far the best backline in the league - even taking their heavy defeat by Brighton into account. While Forest head coach Oliver Glasner has work to do to get his side scoring goals, he's already instilled a solid foundation to build from at the back, as has Andoni Iraola at Liverpool. There's a lot of construction work needed in the capital as Crystal Palace, Fulham and Chelsea have all been far too open at the back so far this season, although Xabi Alonso's side are not quite as terrible as the 12 goals they've conceded suggests. Brighton's brilliance going forward has come at the cost of them not being particularly solid in defence, with Fabian Hurzeler's team perhaps a little fortunate not to have conceded more often. Everton and Leeds have also conceded three goals fewer than expected given the chances they've faced, although both sides have been among the strongest defensively overall. Just five games into the new campaign, it's too early to be making any concrete claims about how sides will perform but their underlying numbers have given us a glimpse of what might be in store this season.
